html:
Kaesong, in the south of today's North Korea, was the capital of the Goryeo dynasty from 919 to 1392. Goryeo, a short form of Goguryeo, is the source of the name Korea.

Wang Geon, a local lord, founded Goryeo in 918 and made his home town the capital the next year. He reunited the peninsula by 936. Kaesong grew into a great city of palaces, Buddhist temples and markets, visited by Chinese and Arab merchants. Goryeo produced celadon pottery, the Tripitaka Koreana and early metal type.

When Joseon took power in 1392, the capital moved to Seoul. The Sonjuk Bridge, where the loyal minister Jeong Mong-ju was murdered by the new dynasty's men, still stands. The palace site, tombs and old academy became a World Heritage Site in 2013. Kaesong later held the joint industrial zone.
sum: Kaesong, in the south of today's North Korea, was the capital of the Goryeo dynasty from 919 to 1392. Goryeo, a short form of Goguryeo, is the source of the name Korea.
